poster_title: Reachability of Independent Sets and Vertex Covers Under Extended Reconfiguration Rules
authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Naoto Ohsaka, Tatsuhiro Suga, Akira Suzuki, Yuma Tamura, and Xiao Zhou
paper_info: National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo, Japan; CyberAgent, Inc., Tokyo, Japan; Graduate School of Information Sciences, Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan; Center for Data-Driven Science and Artificial Intelligence, Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan

panels.headline: Reconfiguration problems involve transforming one feasible solution into another via a sequence of feasible intermediate solutions.
content: Three standard reconfiguration models: token jumping (TJ), token sliding (TS), and token addition/removal (TAR).
These problems have been extensively studied in theoretical computer science, particularly for graph problems.
The study aims to extend the understanding of reconfiguration rules in practical scenarios.
The focus is on the computational complexity of Independent Set Reconfiguration (ISR) and Vertex Cover Reconfiguration (VCR).
The research introduces more flexible reconfiguration rules: k-Token Jumping (k-TJ) and k-Token Sliding (k-TS).

panels.headline: Conventional reconfiguration rules may be too restrictive for practical scenarios.
content: The computational complexity of reconfiguration problems under more flexible rules is not well understood.
The study investigates the complexity of ISR and VCR under k-TJ and k-TS models.
The parameter µ = |I| - k is introduced to analyze the complexity of ISR, where |I| is the size of the initial independent set.

panels.headline: Analyze the computational complexity of ISR and VCR under k-TJ and k-TS models.
content: k-TJ allows up to k vertices to be replaced simultaneously, while k-TS requires a perfect matching between removed and added vertices.
The impact of the parameter µ on the complexity of ISR is investigated.

panels.headline: Examine the complexity of ISR and VCR on various graph classes, including planar graphs, graphs of maximum degree 3, and perfect graphs.
content: Parameterize the complexity of the problems by µ, the guaranteed value, and analyze the results for different values of µ.
The results are summarized in comparison tables for different graph classes and values of k.
panels.figure_caption: Table 1: The complexity of ISR under k-TJ for various graph classes and values of k.

panels.headline: ISR under k-TJ with k = |I| - µ remains NP-hard for any fixed positive integer µ and for graphs of maximum degree 3 or planar graphs of maximum degree 4.
content: VCR under k-TJ is in XP when parameterized by µ = |S| - k, where |S| is the size of the initial vertex cover.
ISR and VCR under both k-TJ and k-TS are PSPACE-complete on several graph classes, for fixed k as well as superconstant k relative to the size of feasible solutions.
panels.figure_caption: Table 2: Comparison between the complexity of ISR and VCR under k-TJ on general graphs and graphs of maximum degree 3.

panels.headline: The computational complexity of ISR and VCR under extended reconfiguration rules varies significantly depending on the graph class and the value of k relative to the size of feasible solutions.
content: The results highlight the importance of considering more flexible reconfiguration rules in practical scenarios.
The study primarily focuses on theoretical analysis and does not provide practical algorithms for solving the reconfiguration problems.
The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the computational complexity of reconfiguration problems.
The research establishes new hardness results for ISR under k-TJ on sparse graphs.
The complexity of VCR under k-TJ and both ISR and VCR under k-TS on various graph classes is classified.
